sampling_model.design: For each analyst-selected \(s\), the assignment law is chosen from all outcome-independent probability distributions on \(\{0,1\}^{2J}\); after pair-preserving symmetrization it is represented by \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J)\).
sampling_model.units: The \(2J\) labelled units and all binary potential outcomes are fixed; only the partition into \(J\) pairs is observed before assignment, while armwise discordance is latent.
sampling_model.treatment: A binary assignment \(A\) is the only source of randomness, and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{jr}=A_{jr}Y_{jr}(1)+(1-A_{jr})Y_{jr}(0)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No marginal positivity restriction is imposed; zero-mass assignment and observation cells are handled by closed quadratic perspectives and explicit primal completions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no sampled nuisances. Nature chooses a fixed schedule in the sensitivity class \(\Theta_{J,s}\); risks, optimal procedures, and confidence sets are reported separately as \(s\) varies.

Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population totals, the minimax bound is attained if and only if inclusion indicators are pairwise independent.
Under within-pair coin flips, the worst compatible binary attributable-effect allocation is a single boundary corner and exact inversion needs logarithmically many binomial tails.

body.tldr: Known pairs are useful when their two units would respond similarly under each arm, but that two-arm similarity is latent. The integer \(s\) is therefore an analyst-selected sensitivity bound, and for every value the project jointly optimizes over all outcome-independent assignment laws and all measurable clipped SATE estimators. A pair-preserving symmetry reduction yields an exact finite conic game, a polynomial-size rational kernel, and dual certificates for the entire invariant optimal-design correspondence; an exact, nondegenerate \(J=2,s=1\) witness rules out the paper-defined paired--Bernoulli mixture workflow. The unrestricted all-design/all-estimator orbit-game layer and the \(J^{-4/3}\) second-order scale overlap with the accepted internal \texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier\_v1} artifact. At \(K=2\), the present hard-discordance class is a structured subclass of that artifact's unrestricted binary class, coinciding with it at \(s=J\), while the pair-preserving group is a subgroup of the full unit-permutation group. The present contribution adds the hard-budget pair geometry, its joint assignment--observation pair kernel, and the exact projected optimal-design correspondence; these are not obtained by direct specialization of the full-permutation quotient, and neither a global extension nor priority is claimed. The sensitivity frontier satisfies \(J R^*(J,s_J)\to\min\{\rho,1/2\}\), while exact finite-minimizer selection on the flat first-order face remains the open \(J^{2/3}\)-critical, \(J^{-4/3}\)-residual problem.

project_justification.gap: The accepted internal \texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier\_v1} artifact already supplies an unrestricted all-design/all-estimator binary response-type orbit game and establishes \(n^{-4/3}\) second-order scaling, so neither generic orbit minimax nor that scale alone is a gap. For \(K=2\) and \(n=2J\), the present schedule class is a structured subclass of its unrestricted binary class, with exact coincidence at \(s=J\), and the pair-preserving action is a subgroup of the full permutation action. What remains untreated is the hard armwise-discordance geometry for \(s<J\): full permutations do not preserve fixed pairing or the discordance cap, so the pair kernel and projected optimal-design correspondence do not follow by direct specialization of the unrestricted quotient. Published endpoint results also cover unrestricted binary schedules and a larger unrestricted bounded-interval class. The superpopulation half-treatment and fixed-design linear-estimator comparators remain non-nested with the present decision problem.
project_justification.niche: The known-pair wreath-product action and hard discordance cap require a finer geometry than the neighboring unrestricted artifact's full unit-permutation quotient. Schedule states are ten-type unordered pair histograms, and the reduced data retain joint assignment-marked observed-pair histograms. Although the underlying \(K=2\) schedule class is a subclass of the unrestricted binary class and agrees with it at \(s=J\), this reduced kernel and its exact projected design correspondence are not direct specializations of the unrestricted quotient.
project_justification.fill: For each selected \(s\), the project supplies the pair-orbit kernel, the primal game and matching least-favourable-prior dual, an if-and-only-if contact certificate for the projected invariant optimal-design correspondence, exact canonicality and uniqueness tests, and a strict rational \(J=2,s=1\) separation with full assignment support, positive active-prior mass, two explicit positive-risk observation cells, and nonzero posterior-estimator variance. It also proves the sharp first-order phase transition and exact inversion, while formulating but not solving the residual \(J^{4/3}\)-scaled epi-limit and exact-minimizer contact problem. The advance is the hard-budget pair geometry inside a structured subclass, not a global extension of or priority claim over the accepted unrestricted artifact.

body.related_work: The closest internal comparison is the accepted artifact \texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier\_v1}. Its \texttt{thm:exact-response-type-game} and the present Theorem 1 overlap at the abstract level where arbitrary outcome-independent designs and arbitrary measurable estimators are symmetrized into finite binary orbit games with least-favourable-prior saddles. With \(K=2\) and \(n=2J\), the present \(\Theta_{J,s}\) is a structured subclass of that artifact's unrestricted binary schedule class and coincides with it when \(s=J\); likewise \(G_J=\mathfrak S_J\ltimes(\mathfrak S_2)^J\) is a subgroup of the full unit-permutation group. Nevertheless, the present pair-orbit kernel is not obtained by directly specializing the artifact's full-permutation quotient, because a general full permutation does not preserve the fixed pairing or the armwise discordance cap. The present quotient therefore uses ten-type latent pair histograms and joint assignment-marked observed-pair histograms and, unlike the neighboring exact-response theorem, explicitly projects the complete contact system onto \(\mathcal Q^*(J,s)\). The artifact's \texttt{thm:first-order-saddle} corresponds to the unrestricted leading-risk layer, whereas the present phase-transition theorem changes that value to \(\min\{\rho,1/2\}\) under the hard budget. Its \texttt{thm:universal-second-order-rate} and \texttt{thm:second-order-rate-and-certificate-frontier} establish the unrestricted \(n^{-4/3}\) order; the present exact-selection question uses that scale only as neighboring evidence for a critical residual problem and does not claim a proved hard-budget Gamma limit. Its rational grid-certificate theorems certify unrestricted values to the second-order scale, whereas the present Theorem 1 supplies the exact finite pair kernel and projected optimal-design face for every \(J,s\). Thus the relationship is structured subclass plus different quotient geometry, not a global extension or a priority claim. Bai2023WhyRandomize supplies the general averaging template, and Kallus2021Optimality shows that structured fixed-estimator criteria may favor mixed designs; neither supplies this hard-budget all-estimator projected face. SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 treats exactly the unrestricted binary endpoint obtained at \(s=J\), and its Airy expansion motivates the residual scale without settling pair-budget selection. Hull2026BoundedOutcomes treats a larger bounded-interval class; the binary endpoint inherits its value and procedure only through the previously stated upper-bound and endpoint-prior lower-bound sandwich. The canonical segment used in Theorem 3 is solely this paper's workflow that convexly mixes paired assignment with the Bernoulli/nonlinear unrestricted prescription and then reoptimizes the estimator; no cited paper is said to advocate that mixture. Bai2022MatchedPairs and deChaisemartin2022Shrinkage remain different, non-nested problems, while HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024, AronowLopatto2026, Wilson2026MatchedBinary, Zhang2026FastBinaryCI, and LiSpertusStark2025 provide design or inference context under different decision classes or assignment mechanisms.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The kernel recurrence and all rational inequalities in Theorem 3 are exact. At active histogram \(20\), every labelled assignment has probability at least \(1/100\), every positive assignment--observation orbit cell has probability at least \(1/100\), both displayed priors put positive mass on that histogram, two named cells each have probability \(9/50\) and make strictly positive risk contributions, and the posterior-mean estimator has a displayed strictly positive variance lower bound. This removes a degeneracy interpretation of the \(37/100000\) separation, but the separation is still proved only at \(J=2,s=1\). Exact row-normalization checks at \(J=2,3,4\) and other projected-face diagnostics remain early-kill computations rather than cross-\(J\) theorems. The first-order van Trees arguments control only the \(J^{-1}\) term; the candidate \(J^{-4/3}\) hard-budget correction still lacks a matching boundary-uniform lower expansion, epi-limit, convergence of minima, and exact-minimizer recovery theorem.
body.honest_scope: The parameter \(s\) is an analyst-selected sensitivity index for latent both-arm discordance, not an observed quantity. For \(K=2\), the present schedule class is a structured subclass of the accepted internal multi-arm artifact's unrestricted binary class and agrees with it at \(s=J\); the pair-preserving group is a subgroup of the full permutation group. The generic unrestricted all-design/all-estimator orbit-game architecture and second-order scale are therefore shared territory. What this paper adds is the hard-discordance pair geometry, whose pair kernel and projected design correspondence are not direct specializations of the full-permutation quotient. The paper claims neither priority for the shared layers nor a global extension of the accepted artifact. At \(s=J\), the class is exactly the unrestricted binary class of SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 and only the endpoint-valued subclass of Hull2026BoundedOutcomes' bounded-interval class. Theorem 3 compares against a paper-defined paired--Bernoulli mixture workflow, not a design recommendation attributed to any cited source. For \(\rho\ge1/2\), exact finite minimizers may select a strict subset of the first-order face; the \(J^{4/3}\)-scaled candidate is not yet a proved limit.
